id: Top:  Cognitive dissonance is like tension in a misaligned gear train: incompatible beliefs pull the system in directions that cannot smoothly coexist. The mind reduces the strain by adjusting, reinterpreting, or discarding one of the conflicting elements until the mechanism runs more smoothly.   Bottom:  A mechanical ratchet is like commitment: each completed step becomes psychologically difficult to reverse, so progress accumulates in one direction. Likewise, a ratchet permits motion tooth by tooth while mechanically preventing backward motion.  Which analogy is better? The one on top or the one on the bottom?
